chapter_mission: Open the book's thematic and character framing: Luke and Mara in their Coruscant sleeping chamber as Luke articulates the paradoxical dream of a dark-hooded enemy who does not yet exist; then cut to Jacen and Ben on Adumar, where their theatrical GA-inspector tour of the Dammant Killers missile factory under guide Testan ke Harran escalates into hidden-stockpile discovery, lightsaber-through-wall breach, firefight with Dammant security, on-camera evidence capture, and escape through the assembly-line portals. Establishes the Jedi-leadership register, the Jacen-Ben field-operative dynamic, and the Allston dialogue-forward voice.
chapter_turn: The book's two engines come online in one chapter: a dark enemy is already moving in the Force (Luke's dream — which the novel's final pages will reveal is Jacen himself), and the Corellian paramilitary infrastructure already extends beyond Corellia's borders (Jacen and Ben recording on-camera evidence at a Dammant Killers missile factory on Adumar).

scene_plan.purpose: Luke sits upright in bed beside Mara and says 'He doesn't exist'; dialogue works through specific candidates for the dream (Raynar Thul in his Temple cell, Luke's own father mid-fall from Anakin into Vader with eyes turning molten gold); Mara's dry one-liner closes the scene; both return to sleep.

Jacen and Ben perform a theatrical GA-inspector tour of the Dammant Killers missile factory on Adumar under guide Testan ke Harran; Ben runs the translator-gag and beard-oil jokes while Jacen Force-reads the guilty thought pointing to the concealed corridor; Ben cuts through the wall with his 'practice' lightsaber; the Dammant security force engages; Jacen deflects bolts while Ben records holocam evidence; the pair escape through the assembly-line portals.

exit_vector: Jacen and Ben escape through the assembly-line portals with holocam evidence — the Adumar fight is joined, not concluded. Next chapter can continue the Adumar thread or cut to another strand.
notes: Matches Aaron Allston's published Chapter 1 of Legacy of the Force: Betrayal. Two scenes: the quiet Luke/Mara bedroom opener, then the long Adumar factory sequence (inspection through escape). Ben's translator-gag, beard-oil jokes, and holocam narration are load-bearing Allston comic beats — they must land. The 'He doesn't exist' paradox and the Anakin-mid-fall candidate are the novel's spine-level setups, both paying off across the nine-book series. Nelani Dinn is NOT in this chapter — she joins the investigation later.
